{{short description|Triangle centers found by trisecting each vertex}}

In [[plane geometry]], the '''Morley centers''' are two special points associated with a [[triangle]]. Both of them are [[triangle center]]s. One of them called '''first Morley center'''<ref name=Clark>{{cite web|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=1st and 2nd Morley centers|url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/tcenters/recent/morley.html|access-date=16 June 2012}}</ref> (or simply, the '''Morley center'''<ref name=ETC>{{cite encyclopedia|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=X(356) = Morley center|url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers|access-date=16 June 2012}}</ref> ) is designated as X(356) in [[Clark Kimberling]]'s [[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]], while the other point called '''second Morley center'''<ref name=Clark/> (or the '''1st Morley–Taylor–Marr Center'''<ref name=ETC/>) is designated as X(357). The two points are also related to [[Morley's trisector theorem]] which was discovered by [[Frank Morley]] in around 1899.
[[File:FirstMorleyCenter.svg|thumb|300px]]
[[File:SecondMorleyCenter.svg|thumb|300px]]

==Definitions==

Let {{math|△''DEF''}} be the triangle formed by the intersections of the adjacent [[Angle trisection|angle trisectors]] of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}. {{math|△''DEF''}} is called the ''Morley triangle'' of {{math|△''ABC''}}. [[Morley's trisector theorem]] states that the Morley triangle of any triangle is always an [[equilateral triangle]]. 

===First Morley center===


Let {{math|△''DEF''}} be the Morley triangle of {{math|△''ABC''}}. The [[centroid]] of {{math|△''DEF''}} is called the ''first Morley center'' of {{math|△''ABC''}}.<ref name=Clark/><ref name=Wolfram>{{cite web|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W|title=Morley Centers|url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/MorleyCenters.html|work=Mathworld – A Wolfram Web Resource|access-date=16 June 2012}}</ref>

===Second Morley center===

Let {{math|△''DEF''}} be the Morley triangle of {{math|△''ABC''}}. Then, the lines {{mvar|AD, BE, CF}} are concurrent. The point of concurrence is called the ''second Morley center'' of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}.<ref name=Clark/><ref name=Wolfram/>

==Trilinear coordinates==
===First Morley center===

The [[trilinear coordinates]] of the first Morley center of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} are <ref name=Clark/>
<math display=block>\cos \tfrac{A}{3} + 2 \cos \tfrac{B}{3} \cos \tfrac{C}{3} : \cos \tfrac{B}{3} + 2 \cos \tfrac{C}{3} \cos \tfrac{A}{3} : \cos \tfrac{C}{3} + 2 \cos \tfrac{A}{3} \cos \tfrac{B}{3}</math>

===Second Morley center===

The trilinear coordinates of the second Morley center are

<math display=block>\sec \tfrac{A}{3} : \sec \tfrac{B}{3} : \sec \tfrac{C}{3}</math>
